mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.5 percentage points over the past 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS changes (p > 0.05 in OLS regression).

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by monthly PAYEMS exceeds 200,000 new jobs, signaling labor market strength that supports equity risk appetite and drives positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In a period of high inflation, PAYEMS growth does not correlate with SPX 20-day returns (Spearman's rho < 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) creates a divergent economic cycle that predicts negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by 10% while INDPRO decreases by 5% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 20 consecutive 5-day windows, the correlation between HOUST-INDPRO divergence and SPX 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 105 over two consecutive months indicates supply-side softness that anticipates positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers without a corresponding rise in SPX 20-day returns (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: When the UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it suggests a tightening labor market that raises policy rate expectations, pushing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns into the negative.
failure_condition: UNRATE remains above 4% for the subsequent 6 months with SPX 60-day returns remaining non-negative (median >= 0).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of accelerating job growth (PAYEMS) above 250,000 suggests momentum in labor market recovery, which drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 50,000 each month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: PAYEMS growth decelerates but SPX 5-day returns do not follow (out-of-sample regression p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in both consumer (HOUST) and business demand (RSAFS) proxies indicates dual tailwinds that produce positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In a high-inflation environment, the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime shift to monetary tightening (as indicated by FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be negative regardless of other macro signals.
failure_condition: In the tightening regime, 60-day forward returns are non-negative in > 60% of instances (complementing the failure condition).
